tldr: Z.ai CEO Jie Tang laid out GLM 5.3's post-training scaling-law approach in mid-August, then the company delayed the release over cybersecurity risks days later without naming a new ship date. A mysterious "Ox Alpha" model then started showing up in benchmarks rivaling DeepSeek, with no confirmed maker.
whats_new: Z.ai confirmed Ox Alpha is its own model — a new GLM-series build — and open-sourced its weights on Aug 27 as GLM-5.3-Flash, quietly shipping the delayed release under a different name.
why_it_matters: Platform engineers who already benchmarked or deployed the unbranded "Ox Alpha" weights should re-map those results to GLM-5.3-Flash and re-check its license and support status now that it has an official identity, rather than treating it as an unverified leak.

status.detail: The delayed GLM 5.3 shipped anyway under the unbranded "Ox Alpha" name; Z.ai has now confirmed it and released the weights as GLM-5.3-Flash, still without disclosing the cybersecurity risk that caused the delay.

open_questions: What specific cybersecurity risk triggered the original delay, and has Z.ai disclosed it?
Does GLM-5.3-Flash carry the full post-training scaling-law approach Jie Tang described, or is it a scoped-down variant?
Will Z.ai release a non-Flash GLM 5.3, or does Ox Alpha/GLM-5.3-Flash replace those plans?
take_for_builders: Re-run any evaluation you did against the unbranded "Ox Alpha" weights using the now-official GLM-5.3-Flash release, and check its license before adopting it as a DeepSeek alternative — Z.ai still hasn't disclosed the security issue that delayed it.
